title: ChronoCulture: Evaluating Cultural Awareness Across Time in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.20472v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Cultural attitudes and social norms evolve over time, yet most cultural benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) treat culture as a static attribute of a country or region. We introduce ChronoCulture, a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal survey data across 72 countries. Each pair contains the same survey question asked in the same country in an older and a newer year, with full population response distributions as ground truth. Across six LLMs, we find that models can often predict a country's attitudes at one point in time but do not reliably capture how those attitudes change. Their predictions for different years tend to stay close together, failing to capture much of the observed change. translated_title: ChronoCulture：评估大语言模型跨时间的文化意识
translated_abstract: 文化态度和社会规范会随时间演变，然而大多数针对大语言模型的文化基准将文化视为国家或地区的静态属性。我们提出了ChronoCulture，这是一个基于72个国家纵向调查数据构建的包含10,360个时间对的基准。每一对包含在同一国家的较早年份和较晚年份提出的相同调查问题，并以完整的人口回答分布作为真实标准（ground truth）。在六个大语言模型上的评估中，我们发现模型通常能够预测一个国家在某一时间点的态度，但无法可靠地捕捉这些态度如何随时间变化。模型对不同年份的预测往往非常接近，未能捕捉到大部分实际观察到的变化。在提示中指定目标年份对提高与调查回答的一致性也没有带来整体上的明显改善。这些发现表明，模型往往呈现出一种基本静态的文化态度图景，凸显了在评估文化意识时纳入时间维度的必要性。
tldr: 提出ChronoCulture基准，利用72个国家纵向调查数据构建的10,360个时间对，揭示大语言模型虽能预测某一时间点的文化态度，却无法可靠捕捉文化态度随时间的动态演变，呈现出静态化的文化图景。
en_tdlr: ChronoCulture, a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal surveys across 72 countries, reveals that LLMs can often predict cultural attitudes at a single point in time but fail to reliably capture how those attitudes change over time.
